questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a typical characteristic of plants produced through vegetative propagation?

options.text: They are genetically identical to the parent.
They show variation in characteristics among offspring.
They flower and fruit earlier than seed-grown plants.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They show variation in characteristics among offspring.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vegetative propagation** is a type of **asexual reproduction** in which new plants are produced from vegetative parts like **roots, stems, and leaves** rather than from seeds.
 
• One of the primary characteristics of this method is that the offspring are **genetically identical** to the parent plant. Because they are produced from a single parent without the fusion of gametes, they are essentially **clones**. ***Hence, statement 1 is a typical characteristic.***
 
• Since this process does not involve the sexual reproductive cycle of a plant, it **does not require pollination** or fertilization to occur. This allows plants to reproduce even in the absence of pollinators like **bees or butterflies**. ***Hence, statement 2 is a typical characteristic.***
 
• **Genetic variation** is a hallmark of **sexual reproduction**, caused by the shuffling of genes during **meiosis** and the combination of DNA from two parents. In vegetative propagation, since only **mitosis** is involved, there is no mechanism for genetic reassortment, and offspring do not show variation. ***Hence, statement 3 is NOT a typical characteristic and is the correct answer.***
 
• Plants produced through vegetative means usually **flower and fruit earlier** than those grown from seeds. Seed-grown plants must undergo a long **juvenile phase** to establish themselves, whereas vegetative propagules (like cuttings or grafts) are often taken from mature plants and retain that maturity. ***Hence, statement 4 is a typical characteristic.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Natural Methods of Vegetative Propagation:**
 
 
• **Roots:** New plants emerge from adventitious buds on the roots, such as in **Sweet Potato** and **Dahlia**.
 
• **Stems:** Modified underground stems like **Tubers** (Potato), **Rhizomes** (Ginger and Turmeric), and **Bulbs** (Onion and Garlic) are common natural propagules.
 
• **Leaves:** Some plants like **Bryophyllum** produce adventitious buds along their leaf margins, which drop to the ground and grow into new individuals.
 
 
 
• **Artificial Methods (Horticulture):**
 
 
• **Cutting:** A piece of the stem or root is placed in the soil to generate a new plant; commonly used for **Roses** and **Sugarcane**.
 
• **Grafting:** Joining a **Scion** (part of one plant) with a **Stock** (rooted part of another) to combine desirable traits, widely used in **Mango** and **Citrus** cultivation.
 
• **Layering:** A branch is bent to the ground and covered with soil to induce root formation while still attached to the parent, used for **Jasmine**.
 
• **Tissue Culture (Micropropagation):** Growing plant cells or tissues in a sterile **nutrient medium** to produce thousands of identical plantlets, often used for **Orchids** and **Bananas**.
 
 
 
• **Advantages and Disadvantages:**
 
 
• The main **advantage** is the preservation of **high-quality traits** across generations and the ability to grow plants that do not produce viable seeds, such as **seedless grapes** or **bananas**.
 
• The primary **disadvantage** is the **lack of genetic diversity**. If the environment changes or a specific disease strikes, the entire population may be equally susceptible, potentially leading to total crop failure.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: When a more reactive metal is placed in the salt solution of a less reactive metal, it:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**displaces the less reactive metal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **displacement reaction** is a type of chemical reaction where a **more reactive metal** displaces a **less reactive metal** from its **salt solution**. This occurs because the more reactive metal has a greater tendency to lose electrons and form positive ions.
 
• The relative reactivity of metals is determined by the **Reactivity Series** (or activity series), which is an arrangement of metals in **descending order** of their chemical activities. Metals at the top of the series, such as **Potassium** and **Sodium**, are highly reactive, while those at the bottom, like **Gold** and **Platinum**, are the least reactive.
 
• During this process, the more reactive metal undergoes **oxidation** as it loses electrons to become an ion in the solution. Conversely, the less reactive metal ion in the salt solution undergoes **reduction** as it gains those electrons to form a neutral metal atom.
 
• A classic example is the reaction between **Iron (Fe)** and **Copper sulfate (CuSO4)** solution. Since **Iron** is more reactive than **Copper**, it displaces the copper from its solution, resulting in the formation of **Ferrous sulfate (FeSO4)** and **Copper (Cu)** metal. ***Hence, the correct answer is that it displaces the less reactive metal.***
 
• If a **less reactive metal** is placed in the salt solution of a **more reactive metal**, no chemical change occurs. For instance, if **Copper** is placed in a **Zinc sulfate** solution, there is **no reaction** because copper is lower than zinc in the reactivity series.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Reactivity Series:**
 
 
• The standard order of reactivity (from most to least reactive) is **Potassium (K)**, **Sodium (Na)**, **Lithium (Li)**, **Calcium (Ca)**, **Magnesium (Mg)**, **Aluminium (Al)**, **Zinc (Zn)**, **Iron (Fe)**, **Tin (Sn)**, **Lead (Pb)**, **Hydrogen (H)**, **Copper (Cu)**, **Mercury (Hg)**, **Silver (Ag)**, and **Gold (Au)**.
 
• **Hydrogen**, although a non-metal, is included in the series because it also forms positive ions and serves as a reference point for comparing the reactivity of metals with **acids** and **water**.
 
 
 
• **Industrial Applications:**
 
 
• **Thermite Reaction:** A displacement reaction where **Aluminium** powder reacts with **Iron(III) oxide** to produce molten iron. This reaction releases a massive amount of heat and is used for welding **railway tracks** and broken machine parts.
 
• **Metal Extraction:** Highly reactive metals like **Sodium** or **Aluminium** are used as **reducing agents** to displace metals like **Chromium** or **Manganese** from their respective oxides during the smelting process.
 
• **Galvanization:** To protect iron from **corrosion**, it is coated with **Zinc**. Because zinc is more reactive, it reacts with environmental oxygen and moisture first (sacrificial protection), effectively displacing the oxidation process away from the iron.
 
 
 
• **Observation of Reactions:**
 
 
• Displacement reactions are often accompanied by a **color change** in the solution. For example, when **Iron** nails are placed in **blue-colored Copper sulfate**, the solution gradually turns **light green** due to the formation of **Iron sulfate**.
 
• Visible deposits also form; in the **Iron-Copper** reaction, a **reddish-brown** layer of copper metal is deposited on the iron nail.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Redox Nature:** Every single displacement reaction is a **Redox reaction**, meaning **Reduction** and **Oxidation** happen simultaneously. The metal that is more reactive is **oxidized**, and the metal ion that is displaced is **reduced**.
 
• **Reaction with Water and Acids:** Metals at the very top (K, Na) react **violently** with **cold water** to produce **Hydrogen gas**, while metals like **Magnesium** react only with **hot water**. Metals below **Hydrogen** in the series do not displace hydrogen from **dilute acids**.
 
• **Chemical Equations:** A general representation is **A + BC → AC + B**, where **A** is more reactive than **B**. If **B** were more reactive than **A**, the reaction would be represented as **A + BC → No Reaction**.

questions.question: A body of mass ‘m’ experiences a force ‘F’, producing an acceleration ‘a’. If the same force acts on a body of mass ‘2m’, the acceleration produced will be:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**a/2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The fundamental principle involved in this problem is **Newton's Second Law of Motion**, which states that the **acceleration** of an object is directly proportional to the **net force** acting on it and inversely proportional to its **mass**.
 
• The mathematical representation of this law is given by the formula **F = ma**, where **F** is the **force** applied, **m** is the **mass** of the body, and **a** is the **acceleration** produced.
 
• In the first case, a body of **mass m** experiences a **force F** and produces an **acceleration a**. This can be written as **a = F / m**.
 
• In the second case, the **same force F** acts on a body of **mass 2m**. Let the new acceleration be **a'**. According to the formula, **a' = F / (2m)**.
 
• By comparing the two equations, we can substitute **F / m** with **a**. Therefore, **a' = (1/2) * (F / m)**, which simplifies to **a' = a / 2**. ***Hence, the acceleration produced will be a/2.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Force (F)**: It is a **vector quantity** that can change the state of rest or motion of a body. The **SI unit** of force is the **Newton (N)**. One Newton is defined as the force required to provide a **mass** of **1 kg** with an **acceleration** of **1 m/s²**.
 
• **Mass (m)**: This is a measure of the amount of matter in an object and is a **scalar quantity**. Its **SI unit** is the **kilogram (kg)**. Mass is also a measure of **inertia**; the greater the mass, the greater the resistance to a change in motion.
 
• **Acceleration (a)**: It is defined as the rate of change of **velocity** with respect to **time**. Like force, it is a **vector quantity**. The **SI unit** for acceleration is **m/s²** (meters per second squared).
 
• **Inverse Relationship**: Under a constant **force**, **acceleration** and **mass** are inversely proportional. This means if you double the **mass**, the **acceleration** becomes half. If you triple the **mass**, the **acceleration** becomes one-third, provided the **force** remains the same.
 
• **Direct Relationship**: For a constant **mass**, the **acceleration** is directly proportional to the applied **force**. Doubling the **force** results in doubling the **acceleration**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Newton's First Law**: Often called the **Law of Inertia**, it states that an object will not change its motion unless acted upon by an **unbalanced force**.
 
• **Newton's Third Law**: It states that for every **action**, there is an **equal and opposite reaction**. These forces always act on two different bodies.
 
• **Weight vs. Mass**: While **mass** is constant regardless of location, **weight** is a **force** (W = mg) that depends on the **acceleration due to gravity (g)**, which is approximately **9.8 m/s²** on Earth.
 
• **Linear Momentum**: Related to the second law, **force** can also be defined as the rate of change of **momentum (p = mv)**. The formula **F = ma** is derived from **F = dp/dt** when the **mass** is constant.
</ul

questions.question: Why is carbon able to form a large number of compounds?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It shows catenation and tetravalency**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Catenation** is the unique ability of **carbon** atoms to form **strong covalent bonds** with other carbon atoms, resulting in the formation of **long chains**, **branched chains**, and **closed ring** structures. This property allows for an almost infinite variety of molecular architectures.
 
• Carbon has a **valency of 4**, known as **tetravalency**. This means it has **four valence electrons** in its outermost shell, enabling it to form four chemical bonds with other atoms like **hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, and halogens**.
 
• The **C-C bond energy** is exceptionally high (approximately **348 kJ/mol**), which makes the structures formed through catenation very **stable** under normal conditions compared to other elements like **Silicon** or **Sulphur**.
 
• Carbon can form **multiple bonds**, including **double bonds** and **triple bonds**, with itself and other electronegative atoms. This versatility significantly multiplies the number of possible chemical combinations and compounds.
 
• Because of these combined factors, carbon is the central element of **Organic Chemistry**, and there are currently over **10 million** known carbon-based compounds recorded by scientists.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bonding Nature:** Carbon predominantly forms **covalent bonds** rather than **ionic bonds**. Removing **four electrons** to form a **C4+ cation** or gaining four to form a **C4- anion** is energetically unfavorable due to the high **ionization energy** and inter-electronic repulsion.
 
• **Atomic Size:** Carbon is a **second-period element** with a **small atomic radius**. This small size allows the nucleus to exert a strong pull on the **shared pair of electrons**, making the resulting covalent bonds very strong and stable.
 
• **Comparison with Silicon:** While **Silicon (Si)** is also **tetravalent** and belongs to the same group (**Group 14**), its catenation tendency is much lower because Si-Si bonds are weaker due to its **larger atomic size** and diffused orbitals.
 
• **Isomerism:** Carbon compounds exhibit **isomerism**, where compounds with the same **molecular formula** have different **structural arrangements**. This phenomenon further increases the diversity of carbon compounds found in nature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Hydrocarbons:** These are the simplest carbon compounds consisting only of **carbon and hydrogen**. They are classified into **Saturated** (alkanes) with **single bonds** and **Unsaturated** (alkenes and alkynes) with **multiple bonds**.
 
• **Functional Groups:** The presence of groups like **hydroxyl (-OH)**, **carboxyl (-COOH)**, and **aldehydes (-CHO)** attached to the carbon skeleton dictates the specific **chemical properties** of the compound, regardless of the chain length.
 
• **Allotropes:** Carbon exists in different physical forms such as **Diamond** (3D network), **Graphite** (layered structure), and **Fullerenes** (spherical/tubular), demonstrating its structural versatility even in its elemental form.
</ul

questions.question: An object of mass 12 kg is located such that its potential energy relative to the ground is 480 J. Assuming g = 10 { m s}⁻² , what is the height (h) of the object?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4 m**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Gravitational Potential Energy (PE)** of an object raised to a certain height is given by the formula: **PE = m × g × h**, where **m** is the **mass**, **g** is the **acceleration due to gravity**, and **h** is the **height**.
 
• In this specific problem, the **mass (m)** of the object is **12 kg**.
 
• The **acceleration due to gravity (g)** is provided as **10 m/s²**.
 
• The **Potential Energy (PE)** relative to the ground is **480 J** (Joules).
 
• To find the **height (h)**, we rearrange the formula: **h = PE / (m × g)**.
 
• By substituting the given values: **h = 480 / (12 × 10)**.
 
• Calculating the denominator: **12 × 10 = 120**.
 
• Final calculation: **h = 480 / 120 = 4**.
 
• Therefore, the object is located at a **height** of **4 m** above the ground. ***Hence, the correct answer is 4 m.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Potential Energy**: This is the energy possessed by an object by virtue of its **position** or **configuration**. In the context of gravity, it represents the **work done** against gravity to lift an object to a specific **height**.
 
• **Mass (m)**: It is a measure of the amount of matter in an object, usually measured in **kilograms (kg)**. In this problem, it is **12 kg**.
 
• **Acceleration due to Gravity (g)**: On the surface of the **Earth**, the standard value of **g** is approximately **9.8 m/s²**, but for simplicity in competitive exams and school level physics, it is often taken as **10 m/s²**.
 
• **Joule (J)**: This is the **SI unit** of **energy** and **work**. One **Joule** is defined as the work done when a force of **one Newton** displaces an object by **one meter**.
 
• **Work-Energy Theorem**: The change in the **potential energy** of an object is equal to the **work done** by the external force in moving the object from the ground to that **height** without changing its **kinetic energy**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Reference Level**: Potential energy is always measured relative to a **reference point**, which in most basic physics problems is the **ground** (where **h = 0**).
 
• **Energy Conversion**: If the object of **12 kg** were allowed to fall from **4 m**, its **Potential Energy** would gradually convert into **Kinetic Energy (KE)**. Just before hitting the ground, its **KE** would be equal to the initial **PE** of **480 J**, assuming no **air resistance**.
 
• **Scalar Quantity**: Energy is a **scalar quantity**, meaning it has **magnitude** but no **direction**. This distinguishes it from **force** or **velocity**, which are **vector quantities**.
 
• **Dimensional Formula**: The dimensional formula for **Potential Energy** is **[M1 L2 T-2]**, which is the same as that for **work** and **torque**.

questions.question: What is the energy absorbed during change of state at constant temperature called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Latent heat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Latent heat** is defined as the heat energy per unit mass required to change the state of a substance without any change in its **temperature**.
 
• The term "latent" originates from the Latin word **latere**, which means **hidden**. This is because the heat added does not manifest as an increase in the temperature of the substance, making it "hidden" from a **thermometer**.
 
• During a phase transition (such as **melting** or **boiling**), the energy supplied is utilized to overcome the **intermolecular forces** of attraction that hold the molecules together in a specific phase.
 
• The mathematical expression for latent heat is **Q = mL**, where **Q** represents the total heat absorbed or released, **m** is the **mass** of the substance, and **L** is the **specific latent heat** of the substance.
 
• There are two primary types of latent heat: **Latent Heat of Fusion** (solid to liquid transition) and **Latent Heat of Vaporization** (liquid to gas transition).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Specific Heat Capacity**:
 
 
• This is the amount of heat energy required to raise the temperature of **one kilogram** (or gram) of a substance by **one degree Celsius** (or Kelvin).
 
• Unlike latent heat, specific heat involves a **temperature change** within a single phase of matter.
 
 
 
• **Thermal Energy**:
 
 
• It refers to the total **internal energy** of a system, which is the sum of the **potential energy** and **kinetic energy** of all the atoms or molecules in that system.
 
• It flows from a body at a higher temperature to a body at a lower temperature in the form of **heat**.
 
 
 
• **Kinetic Energy**:
 
 
• In thermodynamics, **Kinetic Energy** is the energy possessed by particles due to their **motion** (vibrational, rotational, or translational).

questions.question: Which of the following trophic levels is occupied by the tertiary consumers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fourth trophic level**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In an **ecosystem**, a **trophic level** represents the specific place or step an organism occupies in a **food chain** based on its source of nutrition or food.
 
• The **First trophic level** is always occupied by **producers** (autotrophs), such as **green plants**, **algae**, and **phytoplankton**, which fix **solar energy** through **photosynthesis**.
 
• The **Second trophic level** consists of **primary consumers** or **herbivores**. These organisms, such as **cows**, **grasshoppers**, and **deer**, feed directly on the producers.
 
• The **Third trophic level** is occupied by **secondary consumers** (primary carnivores). These are animals that eat herbivores, including species like **frogs**, **small fish**, and **birds**.
 
• The **Fourth trophic level** is occupied by **tertiary consumers**, also known as **secondary carnivores** or **top carnivores**. These organisms prey on secondary consumers and are often the **apex predators** in their environment. Examples include **lions**, **tigers**, **eagles**, and **snakes**. ***Hence, the correct answer is the fourth trophic level.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Energy Flow and the 10% Law**:
 
 
• The flow of energy in an **ecosystem** is **unidirectional**, moving from lower to higher trophic levels.
 
• According to the **10% Law** proposed by **Raymond Lindeman** in **1942**, only about **10 percent** of the energy available at one trophic level is transferred to the next higher level. The remaining **90 percent** is lost as **heat** during respiration and other metabolic processes.
 
 
 
• **Ecological Pyramids**:
 
 
• Concept introduced by **Charles Elton** in **1927**, these pyramids represent the relationship between different trophic levels in terms of **number**, **biomass**, or **energy**.
 
• The **Pyramid of Energy** is **always upright** because energy is progressively lost as heat at each step.
 
• The **Pyramid of Biomass** can be **inverted** in aquatic ecosystems where the biomass of **phytoplankton** (producers) is less than the biomass of **fishes** (consumers).
 
 
 
• **Biological Magnification (Biomagnification)**:
 
 
• This refers to the increase in the concentration of **toxic substances** (like **DDT** or **mercury**) at successive trophic levels.
 
• Since these chemicals cannot be metabolized or excreted, they accumulate, reaching the **highest concentration** in **tertiary consumers** or **top carnivores**.
 
 
 
• **Decomposers**:
 
 
• Organisms like **bacteria** and **fungi** are known as **saprotrophs** or **decomposers**. While they are crucial for **nutrient cycling**, they are generally not assigned a single numerical trophic level in simple food chain diagrams as they feed on dead matter from all levels.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The number of trophic levels in a food chain is usually restricted to **four or five** because the energy transfer becomes too low to support a viable population at higher levels.
 
• **Omnivores**, such as **humans** and **bears**, can occupy more than one trophic level simultaneously depending on what they consume.
 
• A **Food Web** provides a more realistic representation of **ecosystem** dynamics than a linear **food chain**, as it shows the multiple feeding relationships between different organisms across various trophic levels.
</ul

questions.question: What does the term 'formula unit mass' refer to?

options.text: Mass of a single proton in an atom
Sum of atomic masses of all atoms in the compound
Mass of one molecule of a covalent compound
Total mass of atoms in one mole of a compound

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sum of atomic masses of all atoms in the compound**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **formula unit mass** of a substance is defined as the **sum of the atomic masses** of all atoms in a formula unit of a compound.
 
• This term is specifically used for substances that are **ionic** in nature, where discrete molecules do not exist. Instead, these substances exist as a **three-dimensional lattice** of ions.
 
• The calculation method for formula unit mass is identical to that of **molecular mass**; the only difference lies in the terminology used for **ionic compounds** versus **covalent compounds**.
 
• It is expressed in **atomic mass units (u)**, where **1 u** is defined as exactly **1/12th** the mass of one atom of **carbon-12**.
 
• For example, in **Sodium Chloride (NaCl)**, the formula unit consists of one **Sodium (Na)** ion and one **Chloride (Cl)** ion. The formula unit mass is calculated by adding the atomic mass of **Na (23 u)** and **Cl (35.5 u)**, resulting in **58.5 u**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Molecular Mass:**
 
 
• This refers to the sum of atomic masses of all atoms in a **molecule** of a substance. It is used for **covalent compounds** like **Water (H2O)** or **Methane (CH4)**.
 
• For **H2O**, the molecular mass is **(2 x 1.008 u) + 16.00 u = 18.016 u**.
 
 
 
• **Atomic Mass:**
 
 
• It is the mass of a **single atom** of a chemical element. It is approximately equivalent to the number of **protons and neutrons** in the nucleus.
 
• The **unified atomic mass unit (u)** is the standard unit used to indicate mass on an atomic or molecular scale.
 
 
 
• **Molar Mass:**
 
 
• This is the mass of **one mole** of a substance (element or compound). It is numerically equal to the atomic or molecular mass but is expressed in **grams per mole (g/mol)**.
 
• One mole contains exactly **6.02214076 x 10^23** elementary entities, a value known as **Avogadro's number**.
 
 
 
• **Ionic Compounds and Lattice Structures:**
 
 
• In compounds like **Calcium Chloride (CaCl2)**, the formula unit mass is calculated as the sum of the atomic mass of **Calcium (40 u)** and twice the atomic mass of **Chlorine (2 x 35.5 u)**, totaling **111 u**.
 
• These compounds do not form individual molecules but rather repeating units in a **crystalline structure**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Relative Atomic Mass:** The atomic masses used in these calculations are **relative** values compared to the **Carbon-12** isotope.
 
• **Stoichiometry:** Understanding formula unit mass is crucial for **stoichiometric calculations** in chemistry, allowing scientists to determine the **mass-to-mole** ratios in chemical reactions.
 
• **Precision:** While whole numbers are often used for simplicity (e.g., **O = 16**), high-precision chemistry uses decimal values (e.g., **O = 15.999**) to account for **isotopic abundance**.
</ul

questions.question: A sound wave has a wavelength of 0.5 { m} and frequency 680 { Hz} . The speed of sound is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**340 m/s**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The speed of a sound wave is defined as the distance a point on the wave, such as a compression or a rarefaction, travels per unit of time. It is mathematically represented by the wave equation: **Speed ($v$) = Frequency ($f$) × Wavelength ($\lambda$)**.
 
• In the given problem, the **frequency ($f$)** of the sound wave is **680 Hz** (which means **680 vibrations per second**).
 
• The **wavelength ($\lambda$)** is provided as **0.5 m**, which represents the distance between two consecutive compressions or rarefactions in the longitudinal wave.
 
• By substituting these values into the formula: **$v = 680 \text{ Hz} \times 0.5 \text{ m}$**.
 
• The calculation results in **340**. Therefore, the speed of the sound wave is **340 m/s**. ***Hence, the correct answer is 340 m/s.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sound Waves:**
 
 
• Sound is a **mechanical wave** that requires a **medium** (solid, liquid, or gas) to propagate. It cannot travel through a **vacuum**.
 
• In air, sound waves are **longitudinal**, meaning the particles of the medium vibrate parallel to the direction of wave propagation.
 
 
 
• **Frequency ($f$):**
 
 
• It is the number of complete waves (or cycles) produced in **one second**. The **SI unit** of frequency is **Hertz (Hz)**.
 
• Humans can typically hear sounds with frequencies ranging from **20 Hz to 20,000 Hz** (the **audible range**).
 
 
 
• **Wavelength ($\lambda$):**
 
 
• It is the linear distance between two successive points in the same phase, such as the distance between two adjacent **compressions** or **rarefactions**. It is measured in **meters (m)**.
 
 
 
• **Speed of Sound in Different Media:**
 
 
• The speed of sound depends on the **elasticity** and **density** of the medium.
 
• Sound travels fastest in **solids** (e.g., **steel** at approx **5960 m/s**), followed by **liquids** (e.g., **water** at approx **1480 m/s**), and slowest in **gases** (e.g., **air** at approx **343 m/s** at **20°C**).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Relationship:** For a constant speed, **frequency** and **wavelength** are **inversely proportional**. If the frequency of a sound wave increases, its wavelength must decrease.
 
• **Effect of Temperature:** The speed of sound in a gas is proportional to the **square root of its absolute temperature** ($v \propto \sqrt{T}$). As the **temperature** increases, the speed of sound also **increases**. In air, the speed increases by approximately **0.6 m/s** for every **1°C** rise in temperature.
 
• **Effect of Humidity:** Sound travels **faster** in **humid air** than in dry air because water vapor is less dense than dry air (nitrogen and oxygen), which reduces the overall density of the air-vapor mixture.
 
• **Mach Number:** This is a dimensionless quantity representing the ratio of the speed of an object to the **speed of sound** in the surrounding medium. If the Mach number is greater than **1**, the object is traveling at **supersonic speed**.
</ul

questions.question: When an object is placed at the focus of a convex lens, the formation of image is ________________.

options.text: on the same side as the object

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**at infinity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When an **object** is placed exactly at the **principal focus (F)** of a **convex lens**, the rays of light starting from the object and passing through the lens become **parallel** to the **principal axis** after **refraction**.
 
• Since **parallel rays** are considered to meet only at **infinity**, the **image** is formed at an **infinite distance** from the lens. ***Hence, the correct answer is at infinity.***
 
• The **nature** of the image formed in this specific case is **real**, **inverted**, and **highly enlarged** (magnified).
 
• This principle is the reverse of the case where **parallel rays** coming from an object at **infinity** converge at the **focus** of the convex lens.
 
• In a **ray diagram**, one ray passes through the **optical center (O)** undeviated, and another ray, starting from the object and traveling parallel to the principal axis, passes through the **focus (F)** on the other side; both these refracted rays emerge parallel to each other.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Convex Lens (Converging Lens):**
 
 
• A **convex lens** is thicker at the **center** than at the **edges**. It is known as a **converging lens** because it converges a beam of parallel light rays.
 
• The **focal length** of a convex lens is always taken as **positive** according to the **Cartesian sign convention**.
 
• **Lens Formula:** The relationship between **object distance (u)**, **image distance (v)**, and **focal length (f)** is given by **1/v - 1/u = 1/f**.
 
 
 
• **Image Formation at Other Positions:**
 
 
• **Between F and O:** The image is **virtual**, **erect**, and **magnified**, formed on the **same side** as the object (used as a magnifying glass).
 
• **At 2F:** The image is formed at **2F** on the other side, and it is **real**, **inverted**, and the **same size** as the object.
 
• **Between F and 2F:** The image is formed **beyond 2F**, and it is **real**, **inverted**, and **magnified**.
 
• **Beyond 2F:** The image is formed **between F and 2F**, and it is **real**, **inverted**, and **diminished**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Linear Magnification (m):** It is the ratio of the **height of the image** to the **height of the object**, expressed as **m = v/u**. For an object at focus, the magnification is **infinite**.
 
• **Optical Center:** The **central point** of the lens through which a ray of light passes **without any deviation**.
 
• **Power of a Lens:** The **reciprocal** of the **focal length** (in meters) is called the **power (P)** of the lens, measured in **Dioptres (D)**. **P = 1/f**.
 
• **Applications:** Convex lenses are used in **spectacles** to correct **Hypermetropia** (long-sightedness), in **cameras**, **microscopes**, and **telescopes**.
</ul

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **atomic number** (represented by the symbol **Z**) of a chemical element is defined as the **total number of protons** found in the **nucleus** of every atom of that element.
 
• It is the fundamental property that determines the **identity** of an element; for example, every atom with **6 protons** is **Carbon**, and every atom with **79 protons** is **Gold**.
 
• The concept was significantly advanced by **Henry Moseley** in **1913**, who used **X-ray spectroscopy** to show that the atomic number is a physical property linked to the **nuclear charge**.
 
• In the **Modern Periodic Table**, elements are arranged in increasing order of their **atomic numbers**, as per the **Modern Periodic Law**.
 
• While the number of **electrons** can change (forming **ions**) and the number of **neutrons** can vary (forming **isotopes**), the **number of protons** remains constant for a specific element. ***Hence, the correct answer is Total number of protons in nucleus.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mass Number (A):**
 
 
• This is the sum of the total number of **protons** and **neutrons** present in the nucleus of an atom. These particles are collectively known as **nucleons**.
 
• The formula is expressed as **A = Z + N**, where **N** is the number of **neutrons**.
 
 
 
• **Isotopes:**
 
 
• These are atoms of the **same element** that possess the same **atomic number** but different **mass numbers** due to a varying number of **neutrons**.
 
• For example, **Hydrogen** has three isotopes: **Protium** (0 neutrons), **Deuterium** (1 neutron), and **Tritium** (2 neutrons).
 
 
 
• **Electrons and Ions:**
 
 
• In a **neutral atom**, the number of **electrons** is equal to the **atomic number** (protons).
 
• When an atom gains or loses electrons, it becomes an **ion** (cation or anion), but its **atomic number** remains **unchanged** because the proton count does not change.
 
 
 
• **Isobars:**
 
 
• These are atoms of **different elements** that have the same **mass number** but different **atomic numbers**. An example is **Calcium** and **Argon**, both having a mass number of **40**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Discovery of Subatomic Particles:**
 
 
• The **Electron** was discovered by **J.J. Thomson** in **1897** through his **cathode ray tube** experiment.
 
• The **Proton** was effectively discovered following **Ernest Rutherford's** **gold foil experiment** in **1911**, which identified the **atomic nucleus**.
 
• The **Neutron** was discovered by **James Chadwick** in **1932**, explaining the additional mass in the nucleus that protons could not account for alone.
 
 
 
• **Chemical Properties:**
 
 
• The **atomic number** determines the **electronic configuration** of an atom, which in turn determines its **chemical behavior** and reactivity.
 
• The number of **valence electrons** (electrons in the outermost shell) is what primarily dictates how an element bonds with others.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: The arithmetic mean of the observations 52, 40, 76, 99, 52, 27, 80, 27 and 24 is:

Let the assumed mean be 50.

Deviations of observations from 50: +2, −10, +26, +49, +2, −23, +30, −23, −26

Sum of deviations = 2 − 10 + 26 + 49 + 2 − 23 + 30 − 23 − 26 = +27

Average deviation = +27 ÷ 9 = +3

Actual Mean = Assumed Mean + Average Deviation = 50 + 3 = 53

**∴ The correct answer is 53.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The observations are: 52, 40, 76, 99, 52, 27, 80, 27 and 24.

Total number of observations (n) = 9

**Formula Used:**

Mean = Sum of observations ÷ Number of observationsAvg = 5

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of observations = 52 + 40 + 76 + 99 + 52 + 27 + 80 + 27 + 24

⇒ Sum of observations = 477

⇒ Mean = 477 ÷ 9

⇒ Mean = 53

**∴ The correct answer is 53.**

Assumed Mean Method

Mean = A + (Σd ÷ N), where A is the assumed mean and d is the deviation of each observation from A. This method simplifies calculations for large numbers.

Weighted Average

Combined Mean

Combined Mean = (n₁x₁ + n₂x₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂), used to find the overall collective average of two or more separate groups.

questions.question: Walking at (5)/(7)th of his normal speed from his home, Shahid is 22 minutes late in reaching his office. The usual time taken by him to cover the distance between his home and his office is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since distance is constant, speed and time are inversely proportional.

Speed ratio (New : Usual) = 5 : 7 ⇒ Time ratio (New : Usual) = 7 : 5.

Difference in time = 7 − 5 = 2 ratio parts, which equals 22 minutes.

1 part = 11 minutes ⇒ Usual time (5 parts) = 5 × 11 = 55 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 55 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
• Home Office Usual Speed = S, Time = T New Speed = 5/7 S, Time = T + 22 Distance is Constant 

**Given:**

New Speed = 5/7 of usual speed.

Shahid is late by 22 minutes, meaning New Time = Usual Time + 22 minutes.

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculation:**

Let the usual speed be S and the usual time be T.

Since the distance remains constant:

⇒ Distance = S × T

⇒ Distance = (5/7)S × (T + 22)

Equating both equations for distance:

⇒ S × T = (5/7)S × (T + 22)

Canceling S from both sides:

⇒ T = 5/7 × (T + 22)

⇒ 7T = 5T + 110

⇒ 2T = 110

⇒ T = 55

**∴ The correct answer is 55 minutes.**

Proportionality of Speed and Time

When distance is constant, speed is inversely proportional to time (S ∝ 1/T). If speed becomes a/b of its original value, time becomes b/a of its original value.

Average Speed

Average speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time. If equal distances are covered at speeds x and y, average speed is 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Relative Speed

For two objects moving in the same direction, Relative Speed = S₁ − S₂. For objects moving in opposite directions, Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂.

questions.question: If a+b+c=0, then the value of (a³+b³+c³)² is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let a = 1, b = 1, and c = −2, which satisfies the condition a + b + c = 0.

Substitute these values into the given expression (a³ + b³ + c³)²:

⇒ (1³ + 1³ + (−2)³)² = (1 + 1 − 8)² = (−6)² = 36

Now check the given options by substituting the same values:

Option 3 gives 9a²b²c² = 9 × 1² × 1² × (−2)² = 9 × 4 = 36, which perfectly matches our result.

**∴ The correct answer is 9a²b²c².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

a + b + c = 0

**Formula Used:**

a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (a + b + c)(a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Substituting a + b + c = 0 into the formula:

⇒ a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (0) × (a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca)

⇒ a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = 0

⇒ a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc

⇒ Squaring both sides of the equation to find the required value:

⇒ (a³ + b³ + c³)² = (3abc)²

⇒ (a³ + b³ + c³)² = 3² × a² × b² × c²

⇒ (a³ + b³ + c³)² = 9a²b²c²

**∴ The correct answer is 9a²b²c².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Standard Algebraic Identity

The most commonly used expansion identity for three variables is: a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (a + b + c)(a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca).

Alternative Form of the Identity

It can also be rewritten using squares as: a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = 1/2 × (a + b + c)[(a − b)² + (b − c)² + (c − a)²].

Special Cases for 3abc

The expression a³ + b³ + c³ equals 3abc if either a + b + c = 0 or a = b = c.

questions.question: Find the HCF of 44, 110 and 198.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The HCF of given numbers always divides the difference between any two of them.

Difference between 110 and 44 = 66.

The HCF must be a factor of 66 (i.e., 66, 33, 22, 11, etc.).

Checking the highest possible factor 22: 44, 110, and 198 are all completely divisible by 22.

**∴ The correct answer is 22.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Numbers: 44, 110, and 198.

**Method Used:**

Prime factorization method. The HCF is the product of the smallest powers of common prime factors.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Prime factorization of 44 = 2 × 2 × 11 = 2² × 11

⇒ Prime factorization of 110 = 2 × 5 × 11

⇒ Prime factorization of 198 = 2 × 3 × 3 × 11 = 2 × 3² × 11

⇒ Common prime factors are 2 and 11.

⇒ Lowest power of 2 is 2¹ and lowest power of 11 is 11¹.

⇒ HCF = 2 × 11

⇒ HCF = 22

**∴ The correct answer is 22.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM is the smallest number that is perfectly divisible by each of the given numbers. It is found by taking the highest powers of all prime factors involved.

Difference Method for HCF

The HCF of any two or more numbers cannot be greater than the difference between any two of the numbers. It is always a factor of their difference.

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are said to be co-prime if their HCF is exactly 1. They do not have any common prime factors.

• Union Home Minister **Amit Shah** unveiled the **Flood Hazard Zonation Atlas** for the state of **Assam** in **June 2025** to enhance the state's preparedness against annual flood disasters.
 
• The atlas has been developed by the **National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC)**, **ISRO**, in collaboration with the **Assam State Disaster Management Authority (ASDMA)**.
 
• It utilizes satellite data acquired over the last **25 years** (from **2000 to 2024**) to identify and categorize flood-prone areas into different risk levels.
 
• This scientific tool is designed to assist **policymakers** and **district administrations** in planning **disaster mitigation**, infrastructure development, and early warning systems.

• The state is situated in the **Brahmaputra** and **Barak** river valleys, making it highly susceptible to **riverine flooding** and **erosion**.

• **Early Warning Systems:** The data from the atlas will be integrated into the **Flood Early Warning System (FLEWS)** to provide real-time alerts to **villages** and **revenue circles**.
 
• **Infrastructure Resilience:** By identifying hazard zones, the state government can avoid constructing **critical infrastructure** like **hospitals**, **schools**, and **power stations** in "Very High" risk areas.

__
 
• In **February 2025**, the **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)** issued a circular introducing the **Blue Category** of industries to classify entities providing **essential environmental services**.
 
• This new category includes facilities such as **Waste-to-Energy plants**, **Common Effluent Treatment Plants (CETPs)**, **Sewage Treatment Plants (STPs)**, and **Common Bio-Medical Waste Treatment Facilities**. ***Hence, the statement regarding essential environmental services is correct.***
 
• The primary objective behind this reclassification is to recognize the **positive environmental footprint** of these services, which were previously categorized under **Red** or **Orange** due to their operational emissions, despite their role in pollution control.
 
• By moving these industries to the **Blue Category**, the government aims to facilitate **Ease of Doing Business** and promote a **Circular Economy** by providing a more supportive regulatory framework for waste management and recycling infrastructure.
 
• The classification helps in distinguishing **pollution-generating industries** from those dedicated to **pollution mitigation and resource recovery**.

__
 
• **Industrial Categorization in India**:
 
 
• The **CPCB** introduced a classification system based on the **Pollution Index (PI)**, which is a number from **0 to 100**. A higher PI indicates a higher degree of pollution potential from the industrial sector.
 
• **Red Category**: Includes industries with a **Pollution Index** score of **60 and above**. These are high-polluting industries like **refineries**, **tanneries**, and **thermal power plants**.
 
• **Orange Category**: Includes industries with a **Pollution Index** score between **41 and 59**. These have a moderate pollution footprint, such as **food processing** or **pharmaceutical formulations**.
 
• **Green Category**: Includes industries with a **Pollution Index** score between **21 and 40**. These are low-polluting industries like **small-scale tea processing** or **poultry farms**.
 
• **White Category**: Includes industries with a **Pollution Index** score up to **20**. These are practically non-polluting and do not require **Consent to Operate (CTO)**, such as **solar power generation** or **IT and software services**.

• **Agni-5** is an **Intercontinental Ballistic Missile (ICBM)** developed indigenously by **DRDO**, capable of striking targets at ranges exceeding **5,000 kilometres**.
 
• The missile is a **three-stage solid-fueled** engine system, designed to carry **nuclear warheads** weighing over **1,000 kg**, significantly enhancing India's second-strike capability.

__
 
• **Evolution of the Agni Series:**
 
 
• The **Agni missile** family is a critical component of India's **minimum credible deterrence**. It began under the **Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme (IGMDP)**, managed by **Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam** in the early **1980s**.
 
• While **Agni-1** had a range of **700 km**, the series evolved through **Agni-2 (2,000 km)**, **Agni-3 (3,000 km)**, and **Agni-4 (4,000 km)**, culminating in the **Agni-5 ICBM**.

• The missile uses a **Ring Laser Gyroscope (RLG)** based high-accuracy **Inertial Navigation System (INS)** and **Micro Navigation System (MINGS)** to reach its target with precision.
 
• Recent advancements in the Agni-5 program include **Multiple Independently Targetable Re-entry Vehicle (MIRV)** technology, which allows a single missile to deliver multiple warheads to different locations.
 
• The **Agni-5** project was led by mission directors and scientists at the **Advanced Systems Laboratory (ASL)**, a premier lab of **DRDO** located in **Hyderabad**.
